title: Translations of SWCCG
text:
'''Translations of SWCCG''' are the language editions of Star Wars CCG. Decipher printed the English game from 1995 through 2001. [[Takara]] published Japanese sets. Further language editions were planned, including German-language and Spanish-language releases, and were later cancelled.<ref name="vp">Diane Tennant, ''House of Cards'', ''The Virginian-Pilot'', Daily Break p. E1 (11 December 1995; TAG 9512090048). Google's public index of the Virginia Tech electronic copy (22 February 2018): [[:File:Virginian_Pilot_House_of_Cards_Google_index_2018-02-22.txt]]. Unique-phrase search: [https://www.google.com/search?q=%22Translating+the+cards+into+German%2C+French%2C+Dutch%2C+Spanish+and+Italian%22 google.com]. Preserved copy: [[:File:Virginian_Pilot_House_of_Cards_Google_unique-phrase_2018-02-22.pdf]]; [https://archive.org/details/swccg-virginian-pilot-house-of-cards-google-index-2018 Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="encyc">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], p.201 (Other Foreign Language Releases). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Wayback, 8 October 2026]. Collecting hub: [https://www.starwarsccg.org/collecting/ starwarsccg.org/collecting/], [https://web.archive.org/web/20261022023930/https://swccg.com/snapshots/pc/collecting.html Internet Archive].</ref>

== Japanese ==

[[Takara]] published Japanese Premiere Limited in April 1997 (black border; 基本カード): 15-card packs and 60-card starters with a Japanese rulebook. Product photos and the Japanese [[Help Me Obi-Wan Kenobi]] Effect-template printing are on [[Premiere Limited]]. Japanese A New Hope, Hoth, and both Two-Player games followed. Anime-style cards were considered for Japan and were not released.<ref name="encyc" />

== Cancelled German release ==

Queens Games was in charge of the German translation. The company pulled the contract after Japanese sales, and the edition was not released. Surviving artifacts are 1998 magazine advertisements (''Offizielles Star Wars Magazin'' #8–#11)<ref name="oswm">[https://jedi-bibliothek.de/datenbank/ausgabe/offizielles-star-wars-magazin-8/ Offizielles Star Wars Magazin #8], Jedi-Bibliothek (14 January 1998). [https://jedi-bibliothek.de/datenbank/ausgabe/offizielles-star-wars-magazin-9/ #9] (15 April 1998); [https://jedi-bibliothek.de/datenbank/ausgabe/offizielles-star-wars-magazin-10/ #10] (15 July 1998); [https://jedi-bibliothek.de/datenbank/ausgabe/offizielles-star-wars-magazin-11/ #11] (10 October 1998). Preserved copies: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009191112/https://jedi-bibliothek.de/datenbank/ausgabe/offizielles-star-wars-magazin-8/ Wayback #8, 9 October 2026]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20241223104218/https://jedi-bibliothek.de/datenbank/ausgabe/offizielles-star-wars-magazin-9/ Wayback #9, 23 December 2024]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20241223104413/https://jedi-bibliothek.de/datenbank/ausgabe/offizielles-star-wars-magazin-10/ Wayback #10, 23 December 2024]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009164751/https://jedi-bibliothek.de/datenbank/ausgabe/offizielles-star-wars-magazin-11/ Wayback #11, 9 October 2026]. Covers: [[:File:Offizielles_Star_Wars_Magazin_8_cover.jpg|#8]]; [[:File:Offizielles_Star_Wars_Magazin_9_cover.jpg|#9]]; [[:File:Offizielles_Star_Wars_Magazin_10_cover.jpg|#10]]; [[:File:Offizielles_Star_Wars_Magazin_11_cover.jpg|#11]]</ref> and a Modern Graphics German two-player rulebook. The full account is on [[Cancelled German release of SWCCG]].<ref name="boardmatt-jp">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1tdmHYND4xc Star Wars CCG - Japanese Card Overview], BoardMatt, guest Andy Talaga (3 April 2022). Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-1tdmHYND4xc Internet Archive]. Advertisement frames: [[:File:OSWM_German_Premiere_ad_BoardMatt_2022.png]]; [[:File:OSWM_German_Premiere_booster_spread.png]].</ref><ref name="boardmatt-col">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4dR5MIPH4h4 Star Wars CCG - Most Interesting and Strangest Things in Our Collections with Special Guest Andy], BoardMatt, guest Andy Talaga (29 May 2022). Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-4dR5MIPH4h4 Internet Archive].</ref>

German players promoted and won the English game. [[Philipp Jacobs]] of Germany won the [[1997 Decipher World Championship]]. [[Bastian Winkelhaus]] of Germany won the 2001 replacement Worlds at FreedomCon. Decipher Squadron Members in Germany included Winfried Sommerfield in Bochum (Red 41 FL) and Michael Krause in Aachen (Red 67). Others were Michael Lierheimer in Langenbach (Red 102) and Lars Malcharek in Duisburg (Red 114).<ref name="sm" />

== Cancelled Spanish release ==

Decipher prepared a Spanish-language [[Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game]] rules booklet for a planned Spanish release. The surviving printer proof, dated 2 July 1998, is on [[Spanish Premiere Two-Player Game rules booklet]].<ref name="fb-sergio">[https://www.facebook.com/groups/starwarsccg/permalink/10159018539903127/ SWCCG Two-Player Game Rulesbook (Spanish).pdf], Sergio Domenech, Star Wars CCG Facebook group (8 September 2021). Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/swccg-spanish-2pg-rules-booklet-1998 Internet Archive]; [[:File:Spanish_Premiere_Two-Player_Game_rules_booklet.pdf]].</ref>

Decipher Squadron Members in Spain promoted the English game. They were [[Sergio Domenech]] in Madrid (Red 49 FL), Guillermo Ruiz in Barcelona (Red 42 / Gold 17), and Unai Herran in Zaragoza (Red 48).<ref name="sm">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/decipher-swccg-squadron-members/ Decipher SWCCG Squadron Members], starwarsccg.org. Fan-site table: [https://www.geocities.ws/plarathas/SMs.html geocities.ws/plarathas/SMs.html]. == Fan translations ==

CardGuide Wiki has a fan checklist of Spanish card titles for Premiere Limited.<ref name="cardguide-es">[https://cardguide.fandom.com/wiki/Premiere_Limited_(Star_Wars_CCG)_(ES) Premiere Limited (Star Wars CCG) (ES)], CardGuide Wiki. [https://cardguide.fandom.com/wiki/Star_Wars_CCG Star Wars CCG] at CardGuide Wiki.</ref> Its titles do not match the 1998 booklet. The booklet prints '''Barrera Imperial''' and leaves Caller, Jawa, Blaster, and LIN-V8K in English. CardGuide uses names such as Imperial Barrera, Ilamador (Caller), Holandés (Dutch), and Beru Estofado (Beru Stew).

Renato Tenorio's 2009 fan translations on the Players Committee site, a Spanish glossary of game terms and a Death Star II rules supplement, call the game '''Juego de Cartas Seleccionables'''. The 1998 booklet uses '''Juego de Cartas Coleccionables (SW-JCC)'''.<ref name="tenorio">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/2019/04/gameterms_en_espanol.pdf Equivalencias inglés – español], Renato Tenorio, version 1.5 (© 2009). [https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/2019/04/ds2_expansion_rules_en_espanol.pdf Death Star II rules supplement (Spanish)], Renato Tenorio (© 2009). Preserved copy of the Death Star II PDF: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009142831/https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/2019/04/ds2_expansion_rules_en_espanol.pdf Wayback, 9 October 2026].
